title: Ссора из-за поцелуя  (A Quarrel Over a Kiss)

segments.t: This is Kukhnya, which means The Kitchen: a Russian comedy set in a smart Moscow restaurant called Claude Monet, where the chef shouts and everyone else tries to get through the shift. In this story, from episode five, the bartender Kostya has just heard that his best friend Max kissed Nastya, the waitress he likes. Max has to talk his way out of it. Listen to it in Russian first, and don't worry about catching every word.
Отвали, или я сломаю тебе нос!
За что? Что я тебе сделал?
Ты вчера целовался с моей девушкой!
Я вчера весь день хотел спать.
Кстати, технически она пока не твоя.
Для меня это не имеет значения.
Между мной и Настей ничего нет!
Я докажу, что она мне безразлична.
Let's go back through it line by line. Kostya is too angry for long sentences, which makes him easy to follow.
'Kostya, hi. Why are you angry?' is the everyday
is the 'you' form of the verb for 'to be angry', and the reflexive ending belongs to the verb, so it stays on in every form.
Отвали, или я сломаю тебе нос!
'Back off, or I will break your nose!' is a rude 'get lost', not
something to say to your boss. Then Russian says 'I will break to-you the nose':
expresses 'to you' and does the work of 'your'.
За что? Что я тебе сделал?
'What for? What did I do to you?' are two short words you say
when you're blamed and can't see why. The second question has the same
Ты вчера целовался с моей девушкой!
'Yesterday you kissed my girl!' In Russian you kiss 'with' someone:
the words take instrumental endings. The base word for 'girl' covers both 'young woman' and 'girlfriend'.
'It was a completely accidental misunderstanding.' Max goes for long, official-sounding words.
comes from the noun for 'a chance' or 'an occasion', and
is the standard term for a misunderstanding.
'You were kissing right in the restaurant!' Now the 'you' is
, Max and Nastya together, and the verb turns plural:
takes a prepositional ending because it says where.
Я вчера весь день хотел спать.
'I wanted to sleep all day yesterday.' , 'the whole day', needs no
little word in front, just as in English.
is the man's form of 'wanted'; Nastya would use the woman's form.
Кстати, технически она пока не твоя.
'By the way, technically she is not yours yet.' represents 'by the way', perfect for
here serves as 'yet' or 'for now', and the same word is also an everyday 'bye'.
Для меня это не имеет значения.
'For me that does not matter.' Word for word: 'for me this not has meaning'.
is a ready-made way to say something doesn't matter.
Между мной и Настей ничего нет!
'There is nothing between me and Nastya!' After
uses two negatives, and in Russian that's correct.
'You betrayed our friendship, Max.' The base word for 'friendship' is built on the word for 'friend'. Here it takes an accusative ending:
because it's the thing being betrayed.
Я докажу, что она мне безразлична.
'I will prove that she translates to nothing to me.' functions as 'I will prove'. Then
, 'indifferent to me', with the prefix for 'without' stuck on the front.
'We will see how you prove it.' which is the word for 'we'll
see', is what you say when you don't believe a word. Max's claim comes back as
, the form for 'you'. Here's the whole quarrel again, without stopping.

Для меня это не имеет значения.

Keep two lines from this one: the short question for when you're blamed and don't know why, and the expression for waving something away. Kostya's last word is a common way to say goodbye, and you'll hear it once more at the end.
